Two tests a reviewer asked for

Follow-up to #4037 (#3936). One closes a shape gap. One admits a widening.

1. The rule was tested, the recorded shape was not

#4037's anti-bypass case used a curl | jq stage. That proves the rule: one non-plumbing stage disqualifies the command. It does not pin the shape the bypass was originally recorded in.

cd <long path> && bash $P/noop.sh && echo done && echo verified && echo pushed
  len=231  flagged=true

The literal string is covered one screen up by the 2026-07-16 regression test, so this was never a live hole. Pinning it inside the plumbing block too means a future edit to isPlumbingStage cannot satisfy its own neighbours while quietly reopening the original one.

2. A widening I did not intend, kept on purpose

cat $P/alpha.log; cat $P/beta.log; cat $P/gamma.log; cat $P/delta-and-more.log
  len=282  no script stage anywhere  flagged=false

Before #4037 this nudged. After it, an all-peeks command is exempt with no script invocation present. That is wider than #3936 argued, though within the letter of its ask, which lists cat|tail|head <path> as an exempt stage shape on its own.

Kept. Reading several files back is the same look-at-what-happened plumbing, and rewriting it as a script file would be worse, not better. The test exists so the next reader knows it was a decision rather than an oversight. That is the whole value of this one: an accident and an intention look identical in a diff, and only a test tells them apart.

Result

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  29 passed (29)   (27 before)
cd src/hooks
npx vitest run src/__tests__/pretool/bash/display-lint.test.ts
No production code changes. Both are assertions about behaviour that already shipped in #4037.
